chunks: From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the thief who steals, so his hand is cut off, then he steals, so his foot is cut off, then he steals again: is there further amputation upon him?

He said: “In the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام: ‘The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم passed on before cutting more than a hand and a foot.’” And ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: “I am indeed ashamed before my Lord that I should not leave him a hand with which he may cleanse himself, or a foot upon which he may walk.”
He said: So I said to him, if a man had his left hand cut off in retaliation, then he stole, what should be done with him? He said: “He is not to be cut, and he is not to be left without a leg.”

He said: I said, then if a man had his right hand cut off in retaliation, and then he cut off another man’s hand, would retaliation be taken from him or not? He said: “He is only left [without further amputation] in the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But as for the rights of people, retaliation is taken from him in all four limbs altogether.”

key_terms.السَّارِقِ: the thief subject to the legal ruling discussed here
key_terms.تُقْطَعُ: is cut off; used for the prescribed amputation penalty
key_terms.حَقِّ اللَّهِ: the right of Allah, referring here to divinely prescribed penal law
key_terms.حُقُوقِ النَّاسِ: the rights of people, for which retaliation is still enforced
key_terms.قِصَاصٍ: legal retaliation for injury in the rights of people
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: the recorded legal source attributed to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: Does repeated theft lead to further amputation after a hand and foot have already been cut?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling regarding repeated theft after the prescribed amputations have already been carried out. It distinguishes between the ḥadd punishments that belong to the right of Allah, in which further cutting is halted after a hand and a foot, and qiṣāṣ in the rights of people, where retaliation remains applicable.
